## Headline

December was the heaviest month of Mira's visible year — $5,987.33 across seventy-six entries — and the shape of it is two stories: the Vancouver trip and the gift list. Deposits held at the usual $5,221.44, so the month closed about $766 in the red, which is what Decembers are for.

## Key findings

Travel was a single line: the $684.30 Air Canada booking on the 2nd for the holiday flights to Vancouver. Gifts spread across four receipts — Indigo Eaton Centre and Type Books Queen West ($136.90 together), a $118.73 Winners pass through the Stockyards, and the Apple Store and Best Buy stops on the 17th and 18th ($307.66) that closed out the list. Dining stayed frequent but small: thirty-one entries for $643.45, mostly the usual Liberty Village coffee rotation.

## Category deep dives

Groceries reached $817.45 across nine runs, front-loaded before the trip and topped up again for the year-end hosting — the two December Loblaws Queen West baskets were $154.31 and $143.36, and the 31st added one more for New Year's Eve. Liquor came to $185.41 over three LCBO stops, two of them in the holiday-hosting window. The quiet stretch is visible from the 20th through the 27th: Mira was at her family's place in Vancouver and the ledger shows exactly three Uber rides and nothing else.

## Alerts

Nothing alarming, one note: the monthly sweep to the Tangerine TFSA was deliberately small — $100 on the 28th — leaving room for the December bills to settle.

## Easy notes

Rent posted on time at $2,150. Subscriptions held flat at $55.72 across the usual five. Toronto Hydro came in at $103.77, the first of the winter-rate bills. Bell Fibe and Rogers were unchanged at $80 and $75.

## Outlook

January usually runs quiet — no travel booked, the gift season done, and the grocery rhythm back to big weekend baskets. The sweep should have room to recover.
